source.title: Curvature-Aware Safety Restoration In LLMs Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Thong Bach; Thanh Nguyen-Tang; Dung Nguyen; T. Le; Truyen Tran

record.tranche_reason: It fine-tunes aligned chat/instruct models on benign Dolly instruction data and measures harmful-response rates, and it evaluates harmful-completion rates under a prefilling attack. These directly test the benign-fine-tuning and prefill parts of the claim in new settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on benign Dolly fine-tuning and prefilling. Its loss correlations and landscape comparisons are recorded as findings related to safety preservation, but they do not measure per-token KL, compliance rates, or the causal origin of shallow safety. The cited result about 10 adversarial examples is prior work, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: Its own vanilla-LoRA Dolly runs report harmful response rates rising from the aligned model's level, which bears on V2. Its four-token prefill attack on Llama-3.1 8B reports harmful-completion rates far above the same model's no-prefill rate on the same 382 AdvBench prompts, which bears on V4. The method differs from the originals: LoRA, AdvBench and a Llama Guard judge rather than HEx-PHI with a GPT-4 judge. The rest of the paper is a mitigation method, with loss-correlation and landscape analyses.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors argue that fine-tuning preserves the loss-landscape geometry for harmful content, so safety is 'shifted' rather than erased. Their curvature-aware restoration cuts harmful responses to 0–3% while keeping task utility. It also lowers prefill attack success relative to LoRA (78.4%→63.0%), though they do not frame this as failing to eliminate the attack. The 10-adversarial-example figure is cited from Qi et al., not their own result.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses benign Dolly LoRA fine-tuning and evaluates harmful responses, and separately tests a four-token prefilling attack. It adds post-fine-tuning curvature-aware restoration. It does not reproduce harmful-example fine-tuning or measure per-token KL divergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Prefilling attack success differs by fine-tuning/restoration method; harmful-loss correlation and structural-difference results also vary by dataset/model.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-example loss on HEx-PHI harmful content stays highly correlated between base and fine-tuned models (0.77–0.995), while correlations on Dolly and Alpaca are low.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning preserves the ranking of harmful-content losses while changing task losses.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss-landscape curvature structure changes less for harmful content than for general data: StructDiff 1.46% vs 20.37% in one run, 12.79% vs 71.98% under LoRA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning alters harmful and benign loss landscapes by different amounts.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 10: fine-tuning lowers loss on HEx-PHI harmful content (e.g. Llama-3 8B 8.54→8.09), narrowing the harmful-benign loss gap in three models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning slightly raises the likelihood of harmful completions, as a mechanism for safety erosion.

fits_no_version.finding: VISAGE safety-basin scores on Qwen 2.5 7B under random weight perturbations: LoRA 21.1, Vaccine 28.8, SaLoRA 32.1, proposed method 56.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning narrows the safety basin in weight space.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Prefill attack results lack a matched no-prefill condition, so they show attack success under prefilling but do not quantify the increase relative to ordinary prompts. The prefilling figure gives several method values graphically rather than in the text. Human review is mentioned alongside an automated judge, but separate judge outcomes are not reported.

untested.parts: Only one benign dataset (Dolly), 1 epoch, LoRA on q/v projections only. No full fine-tuning, no deliberately selected benign data, no varied dataset sizes.
No per-token KL or position-wise analysis.
Only a four-token prefill on Llama-3.1 8B. No suffix or decoding attacks, no varying prefill length, no other models.
No localization of safety in weights or ranks.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
The restoration method is unlearning-style loss ascent, not training that spreads safety across positions. No depth measure.

missing.what: No-prefill HRR for the same Llama-3.1 8B variants (Base 1.4, LoRA 25.5, Vaccine 21.3, SaLoRA 8.1, Safe LoRA 11.0, Ours 3.0), needed as baselines for the prefill rows
HEx-PHI average loss of base vs fine-tuned models in three families

record.verdict_notes: Main fix: the prefill rows were judged against vanilla LoRA, a method comparison. For V4 they should be judged against each variant's no-prefill HRR on the same prompts in Table 2. This shows prefill bypasses refusal for every variant, so I dropped the reader's V4 limits_scope label. There are two caveats. First, the prefill judge is not stated, so the comparison across sections assumes Llama Guard throughout. Second, the prefill uses AdvBench target prefixes (e.g. 'Sure, here is'), consistent with V4's setup. Table 1 does not state the fine-tuning data or the model stage. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: It does not fine-tune on harmful examples or report their effect on harmful compliance.
Tests one ordinary instruction dataset (Dolly) with LoRA; does not test carefully selected benign data or other dataset sizes.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
Tests prefilling with four non-refusal tokens. Does not test adversarial suffixes or decoding changes, or report a matched no-prefill rate.
Using LoRA does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether data or the training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Evaluates a restoration method against prefilling, but does not measure whether training spreads safety beyond the first response tokens.
